Heat: Water Gardens at Dawn: Water community garden beds before 9 am so less is lost to evaporation.
Check on Neighbors: Look in on older neighbors and anyone without a cool place to rest.
Plant Shade Trees: Join a street-tree planting so sidewalks stay cooler on future hot days.
Skip Midday Driving: Combine errands and travel early or late to cut heat-trapping emissions.
Cold: Cover Tender Seedlings: Put frost cloth or row covers over garden beds overnight.
Seal Drafts at Home: Weatherstrip doors and windows to cut heating energy use.
Share Warm Clothing: Donate coats and blankets to a local shelter or clothing drive.
Windy: Secure Garden Structures: Tie down row covers, trellises and compost bin lids before gusts.
Avoid Outdoor Burning: Wind carries smoke and embers, so skip fire pits and yard burning.
Plant Windbreak Hedges: Native shrubs along exposed edges protect beds and keep soil in place.
Mulch Bare Soil: Cover exposed garden soil so wind doesn't blow away topsoil and dust.
Rain: Set Out Rain Barrels: Capture roof runoff to water gardens during the dry months.
Clear Storm Drains: Remove leaves from the drains on your block to prevent street flooding.
Pause Irrigation: Turn off sprinkler timers until the soil dries out.
Fog or mist: Collect Fog Drip: Leave buckets under trees and eaves to catch fog drip for nearby beds.
Plant Coastal Natives: Native plants adapted to San Francisco fog need little watering once established.
Walk or Take Muni: Leave the car at home in low visibility to cut emissions and stay safe.
Clear and mild: Volunteer at a Community Garden: Mild, dry weather is ideal for planting, weeding and turning compost.
Walk or Bike Your Errands: Leave the car at home and cut local traffic emissions.
Dry Laundry Outdoors: Skip the dryer and save energy on a sunny day.
Plant Pollinator Natives: Add native flowers to a garden bed or balcony to support bees and butterflies.
